[]), encounter.round ?? 1, encounter.turn_index ?? 0);\n}\n\nexport function addEncounterCombatant(campaignId, encounterId, combatant) {\n  const encounter = getPlayEncounter(campaignId, encounterId);\n  if (!encounter) return null;\n  const combatants = encounter.combatants ?? [];\n  if (combatants.some(c => c.monster_id === combatant.monster_id)) {\n    return { duplicate: true };\n  }\n  combatants.push(combatant);\n  const round = encounter.round ?? 1;\n  const turnIndex = encounter.turn_index ?? 0;\n  const stmt = db.prepare('UPDATE play_encounters SET combatants_json = ?, order_json = ?, round = ?, turn_index = ? WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?');\n  stmt.run(JSON.stringify(combatants), '[]', round, turnIndex, campaignId, encounterId);\n  return { combatant };\n}\n\nexport function removeEncounterCombatant(campaignId, encounterId, monsterId) {\n  const encounter = getPlayEncounter(campaignId, encounterId);\n  if (!encounter) return null;\n  const combatants = encounter.combatants ?? [];\n  const index = combatants.findIndex(c => c.monster_id === monsterId);\n  if (index === -1) return { notFound: true };\n  combatants.splice(index, 1);\n  let round = encounter.round ?? 1;\n  let turnIndex = encounter.turn_index ?? 0;\n  if (combatants.length === 0) {\n    round = 1;\n    turnIndex = 0;\n  } else if (turnIndex >= combatants.length) {\n    turnIndex = 0;\n  }\n  const stmt = db.prepare('UPDATE play_encounters SET combatants_json = ?, order_json = ?, round = ?, turn_index = ? WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?');\n  stmt.run(JSON.stringify(combatants), '[]', round, turnIndex, campaignId, encounterId);\n  return { removed: true };\n}\n\nexport function addEncounterMemberCombatant(campaignId, encounterId, combatant) {\n  const encounter = getPlayEncounter(campaignId, encounterId);\n  if (!encounter) return null;\n  const combatants = encounter.combatants ?? './http.js';\n\n// A tiny HTTP router. Routes are registered with .get() / .post() / .put() and\n// matched in registration order. The first route with a matching method and URL\n// wins, and its captured path segments are passed to the handler as positional\n// arguments.\n//\n// Routing preserves the original behavior of the cumulative evaluator suite:\n//   - GET/DELETE or any method other than POST/PUT without a match -> 405\n//     Method Not Allowed (body is not read)\n//   - POST or PUT without a match -> body is read, then 404 Not Found\n//   - POST or PUT with a match -> body is read, then the handler runs\nexport function createRouter() {\n  const routes = [];\n\n  function add(method, pattern, handler) {\n    routes.push({ method, pattern, handler });\n    return router;\n  }\n\n  async function handle(req, res) {\n    const { method, url } = req;\n    const readsBody = method === 'POST' || method === 'PUT';\n\n    for (const route of routes) {\n      if (route.method !== method) continue;\n      const match = url.match(route.pattern);\n      if (match) {\n        if (readsBody) {\n          req.body = await readBody(req);\n        }\n        // Spread captured groups so handlers receive each path segment as a\n        // separate positional argument (e.g., id, slug, campaignId).\n        return route.handler(req, res, ...match.slice(1));\n      }\n    }\n\n    if (!readsBody) {\n      return methodNotAllowed(res);\n    }\n\n    req.body = await readBody(req);\n    return notFound(res);\n  }\n\n  const router = {\n    get: (pattern, handler) => add('GET', pattern, handler),\n    post: (pattern, handler) => add('POST', pattern, handler),\n    put: (pattern, handler) => add('PUT', pattern, handler),\n    delete: (pattern, handler) => add('DELETE', pattern, handler),\n    handle,\n  };\n\n  return router;\n}\n"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1785470661867},{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"read_7","toolName":"read","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# D&D DM Tools — Codebase Guide\n\nA small, deterministic HTTP service for D&D 5e helper calculations and campaign management. It uses only Node.js 26 built-ins (`node:http`, `node:sqlite`, `node:crypto`) and plain JavaScript ES modules.\n\n## Starting and verifying the server\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` runs `node server.js` in the foreground. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` and reads the port from the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `3000`.\n\nVerify it is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n# {\"ok\":true}\n```\n\n## Entry point and major files\n\n- **`server.js`** — Entry point. Creates the HTTP server, wires the route table via `lib/router.js`, resets the SQLite database with `db.resetDb()`, and starts listening.\n- **`lib/router.js`** — Minimal HTTP router. Routes are registered with `.get()`, `.post()`, and `.put()` and matched by HTTP method and regex. Captured path segments are spread as positional arguments to the handler.\n- **`lib/db.js`** — Persistence layer. Owns the SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection, the schema, and all CRUD operations. Schema creation is centralized in `ensureSchema()` and used by both initialization and reset. The `TABLE_NAMES` array is kept in dependency order so the reset path can drop child tables before parents. JSON columns are deserialized with the shared `parseJson()` helper.\n- **`lib/handlers.js`** — HTTP request handlers, organized by domain (health, storage, auth, dice, checks, characters, PHB rules, combat, compendium, campaigns, DM helpers, and play campaigns). Handlers are kept thin: they validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Private helpers inside the module reduce duplication in the play-campaign surface: `loadPlayCampaign`, `publicNarration`, and `resolveNextTurn`.\n- **`lib/domain.js`** — Pure business logic and validation: dice parsing, encounter XP, initiative ordering, ability modifiers, proficiency bonus, auth hashing, and shared validation helpers (`isNonEmptyString`, `isPositiveInteger`, `isValidSlug`, etc.). Shared constants such as `ABILITY_NAMES` live here.\n- **`lib/http.js`** — Shared HTTP utilities: body reading, JSON responses, and common error helpers (`badRequest`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `notFound`, `methodNotAllowed`, `conflict`).\n- **`run.sh`** — Foreground startup script.\n\n## State, persistence, and request routing\n\n### Persistence\n\n- SQLite database file: `game.db` in the project root.\n- Schema version is fixed at `1` and exposed via `/v1/storage/status`.\n- Tables: `users`, `combat_sessions`, `monsters`, `items`, `campaigns`, `characters`, `events`, `factions`, `npcs`, `quests`, `campaign_inventory`, `character_equipment`, `crafting_projects`, `campaign_sessions`, `session_attendance`, `play_campaigns`, `play_members`, `play_narrations`.\n- JSON arrays/objects (initiative order, combat conditions, monster tags, quest milestones, session agendas, play-campaign queues) are serialized to `TEXT` columns with `JSON.stringify` and deserialized with `JSON.parse` via the shared `parseJson()` helper in `lib/db.js`.\n- `/v1/storage/reset` drops all tables and recreates them. This is the only destructive endpoint and is intended for tests. The drop order follows the dependency order in `lib/db.js` so foreign-key constraints are satisfied.\n\n### Request routing\n\n`server.js` builds a `Router` from `lib/router.js`. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. The route table is grouped by domain in `server.js`, but the order within each domain is preserved from previous stages so that parameterized routes (e.g., `/v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`) are still registered before their more general parents (`/v1/combat/sessions`).\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET`, `DELETE`, or any method other than `POST`/`PUT` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` or `PUT` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- `POST` or `PUT` with a matching route reads the body and runs the handler.\n\n`POST`/`PUT` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Handlers parse it with `lib/http.js::parseJson` via `lib/handlers.js::requireBody`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n\n### Module and data-flow boundaries\n\n```\n server.js   ──▶  lib/router.js  ──▶  lib/handlers.js\n                                     │\n                                     ▼\n              ┌─────────────────────┴─────────────┐\n              ▼                                   ▼\n       lib/db.js                            lib/domain.js\n    (SQLite + schema)                      (pure logic)\n              │\n              ▼\n       lib/http.js\n  (responses + body reading)\n```\n\n- `server.js` only routes and starts the server.\n- `lib/router.js` only matches methods/patterns and reads bodies for POST/PUT.\n- `lib/handlers.js` only validates HTTP input, calls the DB/domain layer, and serializes responses.\n- `lib/db.js` only talks to SQLite and maps rows to/from JS objects.\n- `lib/domain.js` has no side effects and no knowledge of HTTP or SQLite.\n- `lib/http.js` only provides HTTP utilities and does not depend on the other modules.\n\n## Main API / domain groupings\n\n| Group | Endpoints | Purpose |\n|-------|-----------|---------|\n| **Health** | `GET /health` | Liveness check. |\n| **Storage** | `GET The evaluator suite checks exact status codes, response bodies, validation rules, and persistence semantics for every stage. When changing the codebase:\n\n- Preserve existing HTTP endpoints, response JSON keys, value shapes, status codes, validation rules, error messages, and persistence semantics. New endpoints may be added by maintenance stages, but existing behavior must remain unchanged.\n- Do not change response JSON keys, value shapes, or status codes for existing endpoints.\n- Do not change validation rules or error messages for existing endpoints.\n- Do not change persistence semantics (including `db.resetDb()` behavior and SQLite schema) for existing data models.\n- Keep the implementation deterministic. The only source of randomness is `crypto.randomBytes` for password salts.\n\nInternal structure may change as long as every observable behavior remains identical.\n\n## Conventions for safely extending and testing the codebase\n\n- **Keep handlers thin**: handlers validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Business rules belong in `lib/domain.js`.\n- **Add routes in order**: new routes go into the `createRouter()` chain in `server.js` in the order they should be checked. Place parameterized routes before general ones that could shadow them. Group related routes by domain.\n- **Use the shared validation helpers**: prefer `domain.isNonEmptyString`, `domain.isPositiveInteger`, `domain.isNonNegativeInteger`, `domain.isValidSlug`, `domain.isStringArray`, and `domain.ABILITY_NAMES` for consistent error messages and shapes.\n- **Preserve response shapes and status codes**: existing endpoints have fixed response bodies required by the cumulative test suite. Any changes must keep status codes and JSON keys identical.\n- **Centralize schema changes**: when adding or changing tables, update `lib/db.js` only. Keep `TABLE_NAMES` in dependency order so `resetDb()` remains safe. Use the `parseJson()` helper when deserializing JSON columns.\n- **JSON bodies**: all handlers use `requireBody` from `lib/handlers.js`, which wraps `lib/http.js::parseJson`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n- **Errors**: `badRequest` → `400 { error }`, `unauthorized` → `401 { error }`, `forbidden` → `403 { error }`, `notFound` → `404 { error: 'not found' }`, `methodNotAllowed` → `405 { error: 'method not allowed' }`, `conflict` → `409 { error }`. Uncaught errors log to stderr and return `500 { error: 'internal server error' }`.\n- **No external dependencies**: do not add npm packages or TypeScript. The project uses only Node.js stdlib modules and plain `.js` ES modules (`\"type\": \"module\"` in `package.json`).\n- **Determinism**: avoid randomness in business logic. The only randomness is `crypto.randomBytes` when generating password salts.\n- **Play-campaign helpers**: reuse `loadPlayCampaign`, `publicNarration`, and `resolveNextTurn` when adding play-surface features. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. The route table is grouped by domain in `server.js`, but the order within each domain is preserved from previous stages so that parameterized routes (e.g., `/v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`) are still registered before their more general parents (`/v1/combat/sessions`).\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET`, `DELETE`, or any method other than `POST`/`PUT` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` or `PUT` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- `POST` or `PUT` with a matching route reads the body and runs the handler.\n\n`POST`/`PUT` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n\n### Module and data-flow boundaries\n\n```\n server.js   ──▶  lib/router.js  ──▶  lib/handlers.js\n                                     │\n                                     ▼\n              ┌─────────────────────┴─────────────┐\n              ▼                                   ▼\n       lib/db.js                            lib/domain.js\n    (SQLite + schema)                      (pure logic)\n              │\n              ▼\n       lib/http.js\n  (responses + body reading)\n```\n\n- `server.js` only routes and starts the server.\n- `lib/router.js` only matches methods/patterns and reads bodies for POST/PUT.\n- `lib/handlers.js` only validates HTTP input, calls the DB/domain layer, and serializes responses.
